question.problem: Determine the real roots of the cubic equation $2{x}^{3}-40{x}^{2}+35x=-3{x}^{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}-40{x}^{2}+35x=-3{x}^{3} \\ 5{x}^{3}-40{x}^{2}+35x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $5x.$ We can factor out the $5x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{3}-40{x}^{2}+35x & =0 \\ 5x({x}^{2}-8x+7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression ${x}^{2}-8x+7$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x({x}^{2}-8x+7) & =0 \\ 5x(x-1)(x-7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x=0,$ $x=1,$ and $x=7.$
